issues: A three star review complained about the takoyaki soy sauce, an older three star review rated food above service, and a further complaint concerned the soba sauce with the same customer rating service very highly.
Saturday service was hectic and sushi fell behind the hot section, so cross section communication has been addressed with the team.
A sushi chef works fast but has ongoing attitude and communication issues with the team, with a formal conversation held and a one week review to 22/09/2026.
Contingency cover is in place if performance does not improve, with a chef returning on 25/10/2026 and another potentially brought in so earned holiday can be taken.
A request to move the sushi start time to 10:00 was previously declined, and there is no active sushi hiring at present.
The kitchen porter area drains are deteriorating daily, are logged as a high priority maintenance job, and a fix was hoped for the following day.
Trade was very quiet at the start of the week and extremely busy over the weekend, with students returning to the city.
Stock counts are inconsistent and are expected to be corrected next week.
Food cost reporting was distorted this week by an AA Factory delivery arriving in the week and an extra spirits order.
Three front of house team members joined or returned in the week and one back of house team member is returning.
A theatre show on the Thursday evening and a Sunday sports fixture are both expected to generate pre and post event trade.

Region-wide (England): The prep level list in the daily Mapal chef report is being replaced by a nightly main protein stock count, recorded on a printed sheet in the kitchen and photographed and uploaded to Mapal every night by whoever closes.

Region-wide (England): The AI daily stock ordering dashboard is only as accurate as the daily stock counts and timely invoice entry into Kobas, and two sites this week showed false shortage flags caused by invoice upload lag.
Region-wide (England): Operations is sourcing a new Char Siu and karaage manufacturer after supplier size inconsistency drove wastage and food cost.
